note: Set B binds the elevation dimensions to the correct elevations far more often: it correctly pairs South Bedroom with 9'-10 1/4" width and 8'-8" height, West Bedroom with 7'-6" and 9'-10", and keeps the scale, revision and artwork notes. Set A repeatedly scrambles values across elevations (8'-8" called North Bedroom, 9'-10" called South Bedroom, 9'-1 7/8" called West Bedroom, 7'-6" called a North Bedroom wall height) and invents attributes such as 'P3 offset from top edge 7"' and 'WB location bottom right'. B does misbind 8'-8 3/8" to South Bedroom and 9'-11 1/4" to East Bedroom, and repeats two facts, but its error rate is much lower. Both sets leave the C1/C5 panel and trim dimensions (P3/P4, D3, W2, door frame trim notes) poorly attributed.
remarks: Text-layer order groups the dimensions into six elevation blocks (C1, C3, C5, A1, A3, A5) but does not label which dimension is width vs height; that mapping was taken from reading order and the drawing layout, so a few single-dimension bindings (e.g. P3 = 7'-2 1/2", P4 = 4'-3", 9'-11 1/4" in A3) remain uncertain in both sets. Set A's 'Interior Elevation E' and Set B's 'Interior Elevation E'/'SOUTH BEDR' show entity-name generation problems (invented letter suffix, truncated heading). Neither set captures the 'DOOR FRAME & WALL TRIM FIN. W/ P4 / P2' finish notes or the MWL01/MWD01/MWD02 component dimensions as bound claims.
